newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: The Philippine peso was little changed on Tuesday as the market awaited further developments in the Thai baht, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.374 to the dollar from 26.373 as volume fell to $150.5 million from $280.2 million.
Traders said the Central Bank was both a buyer and seller of dollars to keep the peso stable.
In early deals, the Central Bank sold $11 million for settlement today to calm banks still wary over the spillover effect of the war between speculators and the Thai government, traders said.
By afternoon, the Central Bank bought $13 million to $17 million at 26.374 for settlement the next day as some dollars flowed in.
"Everybody is selling dollars definitely," a dealer said, citing the Central Bank's high overnight borrowing rate of 15 percent which was meant to protect the peso from speculation.
Traders said the Central Bank may maintain its closedly-watched rate for another week since the Thai baht's problems may extend for a few more months.
"Central Bank's hands are tied. He has to contend with what's happening in Thailand but he also wants to bring down interest rates," a dealer said.
